correctness.rationale: The strictly positive principal eigenfunction yields a principal Prüfer angle with slope \(-t\) on every free interval. Each positive jump advances the phase by no more than \(2\arctan(a/(2t))\), with unique equality at centered logarithmic slopes. Summation bounds t by a unique positive root. Constructing all gaps from phase half-shifts yields a strictly positive eigenfunction, proving attainment; equality in every jump fixes all gaps uniquely. The independent transfer-matrix checker passed 1260 groups but cannot substitute for this all-parameter argument.

value.rationale: Maximizing the slowest exponential diffusion survival-decay rate is a direct physical trap-placement objective. For arbitrary N and unequal, individually non-tradable point-trap strengths, the exact globally unique positions are determined by local adjacent nonlinear phase half-shifts and two independent Robin endpoint losses. This is a complete natural finite-size design classification, not a special numerical instance or trivial relabeling of equidistant equal-coupling configurations.
